Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

shall verb

shall I …? asking what to do

also shall we …?, should I …?, what shall I do?, am I to …?, do you want me to …?

classical

Ter. Eun. 46: Quid igitur faciam? nōn eam?
Ter. Eun. 49: Redeam? nōn, sī mē obsecret.

quid faciam?

the present subjunctive in a question, negative nōn; of the past, the imperfect subjunctive

what shall I do? what am I to do?

Asking oneself or another what to do puts the verb in the subjunctive. Of the past: Quid facerem?, what was I to do? (Ter. Eun. 831).

Other words

  • vīn' (+ subjunctive) — shall I …? do you want me to …? (offering)

    vīn' (vīsne) with a bare subjunctive · also used · classical · Plaut. Pers. 575b: Vīn' hūc vocem?; Plaut. Stich. 486: vīn' ad tē ad cēnam veniam?

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    The offer of comedy; see want for volō with the subjunctive.

Examples

  • Quid igitur faciam? nōn eam?

    So what shall I do? Not go?Ter. Eun. 46

  • Exclūsit: revocat. Redeam? nōn, sī mē obsecret.

    She shut me out; now she calls me back. Shall I go back? No, not if she begs me.Ter. Eun. 49

  • Vīn' hūc vocem?

    Shall I call him over?Plaut. Pers. 575b

  • vīn' ad tē ad cēnam veniam? — Sī possim, velim.

    Shall I come to dinner at your house? — I’d like that, if I could manage it.Plaut. Stich. 486–486b

  • ‘quantum’ inquis ‘prōficiam?’ quantum temptāveris

    “How far shall I get?” you ask. As far as you try.Sen. Ep. 76.5

  • Tua culpa. — Quid agerem? — Adulēscentī mōrem gestum oportuit.

    Your fault. — What was I to do? — You should have humoured the young man.Ter. Ad. 214–214c

See also let’s, should, want, will.

Terence and Plautus checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026): the Eunuchus in the Oxford numbering, which runs one line ahead of Parry’s in that play from about line 390 (so Parry’s 830 is line 831); Terence is spelled as in the loci collections (adulēscentī for Parry’s adolescenti).
